card.name: Adumu (Maasai jumping dance)
card.tagline: Maasai warriors' competitive vertical jumping dance
card.profile: Adumu (from the Maa verb meaning 'to jump') is the Maasai jumping dance performed by young warriors (morani) of Kenya and Tanzania (Wikipedia). It forms part of the Eunoto coming-of-age ceremony, which usually involves ten or more days of singing, dancing and rituals as junior warriors transition to senior-warrior status (Jacada Travel). Dancers form a circle and take turns leaping straight up with a stiff posture, heels never touching the ground, while companions raise the pitch of their chant in time with the height of each jump (Wikipedia; Jacada Travel).
card.insight: The height and grace of a warrior's leap signals strength and desirability to onlooking young women, making Adumu both a display of physical prowess and a courtship element within the Eunoto rite (Lughayangu; African Safaris).
